subject: atlas
summary: Atlas shows live radar and wind on a map, on the web and on phones. It turns public NOAA model data into picture frames every hour and serves them from a cache. Nobody signs in and nothing personal is kept.

blocks.text: Atlas gives anyone a current picture of the weather over a map: where it is raining, how the wind moves, what is forecast for a point, and which alerts are active. It exists so that public forecast data is usable at a glance, without an account.

blocks.title: In scope
items: Radar and wind frames for the continental United States
A forecast for any tapped point
Web, iOS and Android from one API

blocks.title: Out of scope
items: Forecasting of our own: Atlas draws what NOAA publishes

blocks.text: One kind of user and three public data sources. Atlas holds no credentials for people.
Two clients read through one CDN. A scheduled worker is the only writer.

blocks.title: Open the map
items: The app loads base-map tiles from Amazon Location Service.
It asks the API for the current frame list.
The API reads the newest complete run from the Frame Catalog.
The app loads each frame through the CDN and plays them in order.

blocks.title: Publish a new run
items: Every hour the Ingest Worker checks NOAA for a new model run.
It downloads the files and renders one frame per layer and time step.
It writes the frames to the Frame Store under the run's own prefix.
Last, it marks the run current in the Frame Catalog.

blocks.title: Tap a point
items: The app sends the coordinates to the API.
The API reads the matching grid cell from the Frame Catalog.
It asks the NWS API for alerts covering the point and returns both.

items.title: NOAA publishes late or not at all
items.mitigation: Keep serving the last complete run and show its age on the map.

items.title: A half-published run reaches viewers
items.mitigation: Write every frame first and mark the run current last, so clients only ever see complete runs.

items.title: Storm-day traffic on a public API
items.mitigation: Cache every API response at the CDN for a short time and throttle per address.

items.title: Everything runs in one region
items.mitigation: Cached frames stay available; the API and ingest stop until the region returns. Accepted for now.
